title: Seventeen years as Henry Mancini's pianist and other studio work
summary: He was Mancini's pianist for seventeen years on pictures, albums and concerts, alongside jingles and dates for Riddle, May and Rugolo, and a staff job at NBC.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: Then I went to work at Universal; I used to do an awful lot of work at Universal. That's where Hank Mancini heard me, and he hired me, and I worked for Hank, not on a... I was his pianist. I worked for him for seventeen years. But all we did was pictures and concerts. So it wasn't like a steady job, you know. Like, if you were to exist on the money you made with Hank Mancini, you'd starve. But whenever you did work with Mancini, you made money. You had a three-day picture, and then the next week you'd make an album of the picture, and then in the meantime he'd do the Hollywood Bowl or the Shrine Auditorium or something like that. And I was his pianist, and I made all his records. That went on for seventeen years.

And in the meantime, I was doing all the rest of this studio work -- jingles and record dates and Nelson Riddle and Billy May and you name it, with everybody...even Pete Rugolo. You name it. I was in there. I was hot. And it was driving me crazy. I finally took a staff job at NBC, and signed up for three years.
